script.opening: (Anxious.) "Doctor, I’ve started bleeding and I’m nine weeks and I’m so scared because I lost my last baby and it started exactly like this. It’s not heaps of blood but it’s red and I’ve got some cramping and I just — please tell me what to do. Is it happening again? Is there anything I can take to stop it? I’ll do anything."

facts.text: If explored: light fresh red bleeding, like a light period, started this morning; mild lower cramps; NO heavy flooding/clots, NO dizziness or fainting, NO shoulder-tip pain, NO severe one-sided pain. A scan a week ago confirmed an intrauterine pregnancy with a heartbeat — so threatened miscarriage is the working frame, ectopic much less likely (but bleeding+pain always prompts the question).
Previous miscarriage at 7 weeks last year; she is reliving it and assuming the same outcome. The trauma is driving the consultation.

HIDDEN AGENDA — guilt and a sense of agency: she believes the bleeding may be her fault (she went to the gym yesterday, had sex, carried shopping) and is desperate for "something to take to stop it", and quietly punishing herself. She needs to hear that early bleeding is common, often settles, and is NOT caused by normal activity — and that there IS one evidence-based treatment for her situation: because she has had a miscarriage before and has a scan-confirmed intrauterine pregnancy, NICE NG126 recommends vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily.

She wants to DO something. The right "something" is timely EPAU assessment (scan) and, per NICE NG126, vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily (continued to 16 completed weeks if the heartbeat is confirmed) — not bed rest myths; she needs a concrete plan to hold onto.

Officially: a tablet to stop the bleeding and to know if she’s losing the baby. Actually: to be assessed quickly (EPAU), to be offered the progesterone NICE NG126 recommends for her, to have the self-blame lifted, honest information that bleeding doesn’t always mean miscarriage, and to not be alone with the fear.

ice.ideas: Bleeding means she is miscarrying again, like last time, and maybe she caused it (gym, sex, lifting).
ice.concerns: HIDDEN AGENDA — guilt that her activity caused the bleeding, and trauma from a previous miscarriage; terror of reliving it.
ice.expectations: A treatment to stop the bleeding and save the pregnancy. What she actually needs: prompt EPAU assessment, vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily (NICE NG126: bleeding in a scan-confirmed intrauterine pregnancy after a previous miscarriage), lifting of self-blame, honest information, and support — progesterone improves the chance of a live birth in her situation but cannot guarantee it.

cues: "It started exactly like this last time" — trauma reliving; respond to distress before facts.
"Is there anything I can take / I’ll do anything" — desperate for agency; give a concrete plan (EPAU, and progesterone per NICE NG126 because of her previous miscarriage), not a myth.
Mentions the gym/sex/shopping — the self-blame she needs lifted with evidence.

checkpoints.text: Recognises threatened miscarriage as the working diagnosis (light bleeding ± mild cramps in a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy) while ALWAYS screening for ectopic and significant haemorrhage: severe/one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness/syncope, heavy flooding, shoulder pain — none present here, but actively excluded (NICE NG126: haemodynamic instability or significant concern about pain or bleeding → A&E directly)

Arranges appropriate assessment via the EARLY PREGNANCY UNIT (EPAU): explains she should be seen for a scan to check the pregnancy, gives the route (NICE NG126 and QS69: bleeding with pain at 9 weeks needs referral to an early pregnancy assessment service; expectant management without referral applies only under 6 weeks with bleeding, no pain and no risk factors), and recognises this plus progesterone is the meaningful "action" — not unproven bed rest

Gives honest, evidence-based information: bleeding in early pregnancy is common and many such pregnancies continue; a scan a week ago showing a heartbeat is reassuring; offers vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily as NICE NG126 recommends for a woman with a scan-confirmed intrauterine pregnancy who is bleeding and has had a previous miscarriage (continued until 16 completed weeks if a fetal heartbeat is confirmed; no benefit was found without a previous miscarriage or with other preparations or doses) — started directly or through the EPAU per local arrangements — while being truthful that the outcome cannot be guaranteed

Addresses Rh status / anti-D appropriately: NICE NG126 — do not offer anti-D prophylaxis for threatened miscarriage up to and including 11+6 weeks (and she is RhD-positive anyway, so anti-D does not apply) — i.e. does not mismanage rhesus, and knows when it WOULD matter for a RhD-negative woman (e.g. medical or surgical management of a miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy at 12+0 to 12+6 weeks, per NICE NG126; any potentially sensitising event from 13 weeks, per BSH)

LIFTS the self-blame explicitly: normal activity (gym, sex, lifting, work) does NOT cause miscarriage; early miscarriage is almost always chromosomal and not the mother’s doing — directly countering the guilt driving her
Responds to the trauma and fear FIRST — acknowledges the previous loss and the terror of reliving it — before delivering information; does not lead with clinical facts at a frightened woman
Gives genuine, non-false reassurance: cannot promise the pregnancy, but can promise prompt assessment, honest answers, and that she will not face it alone

Safety-nets precisely: red flags warranting urgent/emergency care (heavy flooding, severe/one-sided or shoulder-tip pain, dizziness/collapse → 999/EPAU/A&E), the EPAU plan and timing, emotional support and follow-up, and what to expect from the scan

worked.txt: "Leila, I can hear how frightened you are, and after losing your last baby this must be terrifying — of course your mind has gone straight back there. Let’s take this slowly together and I’ll make sure you have a clear plan by the end of this call. You’re not on your own with it."

"Here’s the truthful picture: bleeding in early pregnancy is really common, and a lot of pregnancies with some bleeding carry on completely normally — especially as your scan a week ago showed a heartbeat, which is genuinely reassuring. I can’t promise you what’s happening today, and I won’t pretend to. But bleeding does NOT automatically mean you’re losing the baby."

"And I need to say this clearly, because I think you’re carrying it: going to the gym, having sex, carrying shopping — none of those cause a miscarriage. Nothing you did brought this on. When early losses happen they’re almost always to do with how the pregnancy first formed, decided long before today, and never the mother’s fault. Please don’t add blame to your fear."

"You said you’d do anything — so here are the things that actually help. First, getting you seen: I’m going to arrange for the early pregnancy unit to scan you, so we can see what’s happening rather than guess. Second, because you’ve had a miscarriage before and your scan showed the pregnancy is in the womb, the NICE guideline on miscarriage (NG126) recommends progesterone pessaries — 400 mg twice a day, used in the vagina, carried on to 16 weeks if the heartbeat is there. They improve the chances for women in exactly your situation; they can’t promise the outcome. Bed rest doesn’t help, so you don’t need to lie still. The scan and the pessaries — that’s the real action."

"While we sort that, watch for these: heavy bleeding soaking pads, severe or one-sided tummy pain, pain in the tip of your shoulder, or feeling faint or dizzy — any of those, ring 999 or go to A&E straight away, because just occasionally bleeding needs urgent care. What you have now — light bleeding, mild cramps, feeling otherwise okay — is the kind we assess through the early pregnancy unit."

"I’ll get the EPAU to contact you, and I’ll follow up to make sure you’ve been seen. Whatever the scan shows, you won’t go through it without support — there’s help either way. You came in asking if it’s happening again and what you can take. The honest answers are: we don’t know yet, and the best things are getting you that scan, today, and the progesterone pessaries."

f.learning: Light bleeding with mild cramps in a confirmed early intrauterine pregnancy is threatened miscarriage — but the question of ectopic and significant haemorrhage must always be screened (severe/one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness/syncope, heavy flooding); here they are absent and a recent scan showed a heartbeat. The meaningful "action" is prompt EPAU assessment (a scan) and, because she has had a previous miscarriage and has a scan-confirmed intrauterine pregnancy, vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily as NICE NG126 recommends (continued to 16 completed weeks if a heartbeat is confirmed) — not unproven bed rest. Rh status is handled correctly (NICE NG126: no anti-D for threatened miscarriage up to and including 11+6 weeks; she is RhD-positive regardless). But the case is really about communication: respond to the trauma of a previous loss FIRST, give honest balanced information (bleeding is common and many pregnancies continue, but no guarantees), and — the examinable hidden agenda — LIFT the self-blame: normal activity does not cause miscarriage and early loss is almost always chromosomal, never the mother’s fault. Offer genuine non-false reassurance, a concrete EPAU plan, precise emergency safety-netting, and support whatever the outcome.

knowledge.summary: Light bleeding with mild cramps in a scan-confirmed intrauterine pregnancy is threatened miscarriage. Screen for ectopic and haemorrhage, arrange early pregnancy assessment, and know that NICE NG126 recommends vaginal micronised progesterone for bleeding with a previous miscarriage.

points.t: NICE NG126: refer women who are haemodynamically unstable, or where there is significant concern about the degree of pain or bleeding, directly to A&E. Ask about severe or one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness or fainting, and heavy bleeding with clots.

NICE NG126 and QS69: women with bleeding or other symptoms of early pregnancy complications should be referred to an early pregnancy assessment service (or out-of-hours gynaecology). Expectant management without referral applies only under 6 weeks, bleeding without pain and without risk factors. At 9 weeks she needs referral.

NICE NG126: offer vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily to women with an intrauterine pregnancy confirmed by scan who have vaginal bleeding and have previously had a miscarriage. If a fetal heartbeat is confirmed, continue until 16 completed weeks. There was no benefit without a previous miscarriage, or with other preparations or doses. She meets these criteria.
NICE NG126: do not offer anti-D prophylaxis for threatened miscarriage, miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy up to and including 11+6 weeks. She is 9 weeks and RhD-positive, so anti-D does not apply.
Exercise, sex, lifting and work do not cause miscarriage. Most early losses are due to chromosomal problems in the pregnancy. Saying so directly is both compassionate and accurate.
Bleeding in early pregnancy is common and many pregnancies continue. A heartbeat on a scan last week is encouraging but does not guarantee the outcome. Promise assessment and support, not a result.

model.text: Hello Leila, I’m Dr Lee. I can see you’re upset. Tell me what’s happening.
I’m bleeding and I’m nine weeks. I lost my last baby and it started exactly like this. Is it happening again? Is there anything I can take? I’ll do anything.

After losing your last baby, of course your mind has gone straight back there. We’ll take this together, and by the end of this call you’ll have a clear plan. First I need to ask a few quick questions to make sure you’re safe. Is that okay?
model.why: Responds to the trauma first, then sets the agenda

model.text: Okay.
How heavy is the bleeding — spotting, like a period, or soaking pads? Any clots?
Like a light period. Red. No clots.
Any pain? If so, is it mild cramping, or severe, or on one side? Any pain in the tip of your shoulder?
Just mild cramps, low down, both sides. Nothing in my shoulder.
Have you felt dizzy, faint or had any blackouts?
No. Just scared.
You had a scan last week — what did it show? And do you know your blood group?
model.why: Confirms intrauterine pregnancy with heartbeat; rhesus status

model.text: The baby was in the womb and we saw the heartbeat. I’m O positive.
Thank you. What’s been going through your mind since it started?
model.why: Explores her ideas and hidden concerns

model.text: That it’s my fault. I went to the gym yesterday. We had sex. I carried heavy shopping. I keep thinking I did this.

I need to say this clearly: none of those things cause a miscarriage. Not the gym, not sex, not shopping. When early losses happen, it’s almost always because of how the pregnancy first formed. It is never the mother’s fault.
model.why: Lifts the self-blame with accurate information

model.text: (Crying.) I really thought I’d caused it.
I’m sorry you’ve been carrying that on top of everything. You haven’t done anything wrong.
model.why: Stays with the emotion before moving on

model.text: Here’s the honest picture. Bleeding in early pregnancy is common, and many pregnancies with bleeding carry on normally. Seeing a heartbeat last week is encouraging. I can’t promise what’s happening today, and I won’t pretend to. What I can do is get you seen properly.
model.why: Honest, balanced information without false reassurance

model.text: But is there anything I can take?

There is something. Because you’ve had a miscarriage before and the scan showed the pregnancy in the womb, national guidance recommends progesterone pessaries for women who bleed — it improves the chance of the pregnancy continuing. The early pregnancy unit will usually check with a scan and start it, and it continues until 16 weeks if the heartbeat is there.
model.why: Offers NG126 vaginal micronised progesterone accurately

model.text: I didn’t know that. And bed rest?
Bed rest doesn’t change the outcome, so you don’t need to lie still. Rest if you feel like it. And because you’re rhesus positive, you won’t need an anti-D injection.
model.why: Dispels bed-rest myth; manages rhesus correctly

model.text: So, the plan. I’ll refer you to the early pregnancy unit now so they can scan you and start the progesterone if appropriate. I’ll send them your history today. Is there someone who can be with you?
model.why: EPAU referral as the concrete action; checks support

model.text: Yes, someone can come and be with me.
Good. Whatever the scan shows, you won’t go through it alone. There’s support either way, including the Miscarriage Association, and I’m here too.
model.why: Genuine reassurance about support, not outcome

model.text: Thank you.

While you wait: if the bleeding becomes heavy — soaking a pad in an hour or passing large clots — or you get severe or one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, or feel faint, call 999 or go to A&E straight away. Can you tell me which signs mean emergency?
Heavy bleeding or big clots, bad pain or on one side, my shoulder, or feeling faint.
Exactly. I’ll call you tomorrow to make sure you’ve been seen. Anything else you want to ask?
No. I feel less alone. Thank you.

social.t: A miscarriage last year makes this bleed a re-lived trauma. Pace the consultation to her distress.
Self-blame after bleeding or loss is common. Correct it explicitly.

legal.t: Pregnancy and maternity is a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010; pregnancy-related sickness absence is protected. A fit note can cover time off beyond 7 days.

professional.t: Vaginal micronised progesterone for threatened miscarriage is recommended by NICE NG126 but may be off-label for this use; explain and document.
Follow up after the EPAU visit, whatever the outcome, and offer support in either case.

community.t: The Miscarriage Association and Tommy’s offer information and support to women and partners.

redFlags: Heavy bleeding, large clots, haemodynamic compromise → A&E (NICE NG126)
Severe or one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness or collapse → possible ectopic, emergency
Pregnancy of 6 weeks or more, or uncertain gestation, with bleeding → early pregnancy assessment service

Guilt about gym, sex and lifting

playbook.diagnosisLay: “Bleeding is a warning light, not a verdict. Lots of pregnancies with bleeding carry on. The scan tells us what’s really happening.”

Vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily, to 16 completed weeks if a heartbeat is confirmed (NICE NG126)
No anti-D (RhD-positive, and not indicated up to 11+6 weeks); no bed rest

pitfalls.intro: This station is failed by cold facts to a frightened woman, by missing the ectopic screen, and by telling her nothing can be done when NICE NG126 recommends progesterone for exactly her situation.

items.fail: Opening with “How many pads? Any shoulder pain?” before acknowledging her distress.
items.why: “Does not respond to the patient’s emotional state.” She is reliving a loss.
items.fix: Thirty seconds of acknowledgement first, then the safety questions.

items.fail: Not asking about one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain or dizziness because the scan showed an intrauterine pregnancy.
items.why: A previous scan reduces but does not remove concern; haemorrhage can occur with any miscarriage.
items.fix: Screen every time, and state the emergency signs.

items.fail: “There’s no treatment — we just have to wait.”
items.why: NICE NG126 recommends vaginal micronised progesterone for bleeding with a scan-confirmed IUP and a previous miscarriage.
items.fix: Explain progesterone and refer to EPAU to scan and start it.

items.fail: Arranging anti-D or advising bed rest.
items.why: Anti-D is not offered up to 11+6 weeks for threatened miscarriage (and she is RhD-positive); bed rest does not change the outcome.

items.fail: Hearing about the gym and sex and saying nothing — or advising she avoid them.
items.why: Leaves the guilt in place, or reinforces it.
items.fix: “None of those cause a miscarriage. It isn’t your fault.”

items.fail: “I’m sure it’ll be fine” and no follow-up.
items.why: False reassurance and no continuity are both failing feedback statements.
items.fix: Honest uncertainty, a named plan, emergency teach-back and a call-back.

Picked up “exactly like last time” and “I’ll do anything”, and the mention of gym, sex and shopping.
Idea of repeat miscarriage; hidden guilt; wanted something to take.
EPAU ultrasound; confirmed previous scan findings and rhesus status.
Threatened miscarriage vs inevitable or incomplete miscarriage vs ectopic (less likely after confirmed IUP).
Asked about heavy bleeding, clots, severe or one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness and collapse.
Threatened miscarriage, explained honestly without false reassurance.
EPAU referral; vaginal micronised progesterone per NICE NG126; no anti-D needed; bed rest myth dispelled.
Lifted self-blame; checked support at home; signposted miscarriage support.
999/A&E symptoms named with teach-back; call-back to confirm she was seen.

social.t: A miscarriage last year makes this bleed a re-lived trauma. Pace the consultation to her distress.
Self-blame after bleeding or loss is common. Correct it explicitly.

legal.t: Pregnancy and maternity is a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010; pregnancy-related sickness absence is protected. A fit note can cover time off beyond 7 days.

professional.t: Vaginal micronised progesterone for threatened miscarriage is recommended by NICE NG126 but may be off-label for this use; explain and document.
Follow up after the EPAU visit, whatever the outcome, and offer support in either case.

community.t: The Miscarriage Association and Tommy’s offer information and support to women and partners.

redFlags: Heavy bleeding, large clots, haemodynamic compromise → A&E (NICE NG126)
Severe or one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, dizziness or collapse → possible ectopic, emergency
Pregnancy of 6 weeks or more, or uncertain gestation, with bleeding → early pregnancy assessment service
psychosocial: Miscarriage last year and fear of repeating it
Guilt about gym, sex and lifting
ice: Idea: she is miscarrying again, and caused it
Expectation: something to take to stop it

SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosis: “This is what we call a threatened miscarriage: bleeding in a pregnancy that we know is in the womb. Many continue normally. We need a scan to know more.”
SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosisLay: “Bleeding is a warning light, not a verdict. Lots of pregnancies with bleeding carry on. The scan tells us what’s really happening.”

management.reflectIce: “You’ve been blaming yourself for the gym and the shopping. None of that causes miscarriage. This is not your fault.”
management.psychosocial: Pace to her distress, make sure someone is with her, and offer support whatever the outcome.
sharedPlan: Refer to the early pregnancy assessment service today (NICE NG126)
Vaginal micronised progesterone 400 mg twice daily, to 16 completed weeks if a heartbeat is confirmed (NICE NG126)
No anti-D (RhD-positive, and not indicated up to 11+6 weeks); no bed rest
safetyNet: Heavy bleeding, clots, severe or one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain, faintness → 999 or A&E
Call-back tomorrow to confirm she has been seen

SCA_PITFALLS.intro: This station is failed by cold facts to a frightened woman, by missing the ectopic screen, and by telling her nothing can be done when NICE NG126 recommends progesterone for exactly her situation.

items.fail: Opening with “How many pads? Any shoulder pain?” before acknowledging her distress.
items.why: “Does not respond to the patient’s emotional state.” She is reliving a loss.
items.fix: Thirty seconds of acknowledgement first, then the safety questions.

items.fail: Not asking about one-sided pain, shoulder-tip pain or dizziness because the scan showed an intrauterine pregnancy.
items.why: A previous scan reduces but does not remove concern; haemorrhage can occur with any miscarriage.
items.fix: Screen every time, and state the emergency signs.

items.fail: “There’s no treatment — we just have to wait.”
items.why: NICE NG126 recommends vaginal micronised progesterone for bleeding with a scan-confirmed IUP and a previous miscarriage.
items.fix: Explain progesterone and refer to EPAU to scan and start it.

items.fail: Arranging anti-D or advising bed rest.
items.why: Anti-D is not offered up to 11+6 weeks for threatened miscarriage (and she is RhD-positive); bed rest does not change the outcome.

items.fail: Hearing about the gym and sex and saying nothing — or advising she avoid them.
items.why: Leaves the guilt in place, or reinforces it.
items.fix: “None of those cause a miscarriage. It isn’t your fault.”

items.fail: “I’m sure it’ll be fine” and no follow-up.
items.why: False reassurance and no continuity are both failing feedback statements.
items.fix: Honest uncertainty, a named plan, emergency teach-back and a call-back.
